chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Abd al-A'la, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah عليه السلام saying: "Listening and obedience are the doors of goodness. The listener who obeys has no proof against him, and the listener who disobeys has no proof for him. And the Imam of the Muslims, his proof and his argument are completed on the Day when he meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic."
Then he said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.’"

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الْخَيْرِ: means and entrances leading to goodness
key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Imam who is the religious leader of the Muslims
key_terms.احْتِجَاجُهُ: his establishing of the argument or proof
key_terms.السَّمْعُ: heeding and listening attentively to rightful authority
key_terms.الطَّاعَةُ: obedience to the divinely appointed command
key_terms.بِإِمَامِهِمْ: with their Imam, by whom people are identified on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.حُجَّةَ: proof, claim, or binding argument before Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain obedience to the Imam and the verse ‘The Day We shall call every people by their Imam’?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that listening and obedience to rightful divine authority are among the gates of goodness, and that obedience removes one's excuse before Allah. It also affirms the centrality of the Imam in the life of the Muslim community and on the Day of Judgment, linking this meaning to the Qur'anic declaration that every people will be called by their Imam.
